header: Date: 2026-04-01 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Alyssa Chen, Marco Diaz, Priya Nair (Redwood) — Daniel Park, Leah Kim, Omar Rahman, Sara Lowe (SignalSoft)
summary: Redwood AE/SE ran a migration & parity demo for SignalSoft, mapping common OpenAI/Anthropic/Together API calls to Redwood API and Console capabilities. Primary focus: model/function parity, streaming & function-calling differences, embeddings/semantic search migration, cost/latency tradeoffs, Dedicated vs Hosted, and security/compliance (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Customer agreed to share prompt sets and run a small POC benchmark; Redwood to provide pricing, parity spreadsheet, and benchmark guide.
topics: Security: VPC, KMS, audit logs, SOC2
transcript: [00:00] Alyssa (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time — quick intros?

[00:07] Daniel (SignalSoft): Hi, Daniel Park here, CTO. Leah and Omar are on; Sara will chime on procurement items. We're mainly interested in moving from a mix of OpenAI and Anthropic to a single provider for inference.

[00:22] Alyssa: Great, appreciate that. Our goal today is a parity walkthrough — show how Redwood maps to common OpenAI/Anthropic/Together flows and where ops + cost wins are. Marco will run the demo.
[00:35] Marco (Redwood SE): Cool — quick FYI, I'll show API calls, Console routes, and Optimize suggestions. We'll also touch Dedicated capacity and VPCs since Omar asked earlier.
[00:47] Leah: Yep that's right — we want to see function-calling parity and embeddings. Also streaming behavior, and whether we can match the latency we get now.

[01:05] Marco: Ok starting with chat parity — Redwood's chat endpoint supports streaming and function/tool-calling similar to OpenAI. Example call: POST /v1/chat/completions maps to /v1/generate with role messages, we can stream chunks and include function schemas. (slight audio) you might see slight naming diffs, like we use 'tools' in Console but OK
[01:38] Daniel: How about TogetherAI models — do they map cleanly? We have some models we call in prod for cost reasons.

[01:45] Marco: We maintain a model catalog. For Together you can pick a compatible Redwood-verified variant; latency/cost profiles are surfaced. There are cases where quantized variants change perf, we'll flag those in the parity sheet.
[02:12] Alyssa: Important: we'll send a parity spreadsheet that lists OpenAI/Anthropic/Together endpoints and exact Redwood equivalents, plus known behavioral diffs.
[02:25] Leah: Perfect — also curious about embeddings. We use OpenAI embeddings for semantic search.

[02:32] Marco: Redwood supports embeddings via a simple embeddings endpoint. We also have the Console's embeddings route which gives token-level cost breakdowns and batch suggestions. Data residency and retention are configurable on Dedicated/Private.
[02:58] Omar: On VPC: we need to ensure we can peer or run in our VPC, and KMS for keys. Any blockers?

[03:06] Priya (Product): For Private or Dedicated we support VPC peering and customer KMS integrations. On hosted, we have tenancy controls and audit logs but not direct peering. We'll capture options in the security doc link.
[03:30] Daniel: Can you show Console rollout / canary behavior? We do several model rollouts across services.

[03:38] Marco: Sure — (screen share) Console > Routes: you can pin model versions, set traffic splits, and configure automatic fallback policies — e.g., fallback to a smaller quantized variant if latency spikes. You can also set per-route cost caps.
[04:11] Marco: Note: when we say 'quantized variant' there can be small sampling diffs; we'll include evals in the POC.
[04:25] Leah: How do you recommend mapping function-calls? We use structured outputs heavily.

[04:31] Marco: Use Redwood's function schema support — same idea as OpenAI function calling. Our SDK has helpers and we show a code snippet that maps OpenAI's function signature to Redwood's call. There's also structured output mode for stricter JSON responses.
[04:55] Alyssa: Quick question on billing — do we do per-token like OpenAI?
[05:02] Marco: Hosted is usage-based per-token/embedding unit; Dedicated is committed capacity with predictable throughput. Optimize can recommend batching/quantization to reduce unit cost.
[05:20] Daniel: Any hard guarantees for latency? We see 80–120ms tail on OpenAI for small prompts.

[05:27] Marco: For Hosted, latency varies by model; we show performance profiles in the Console. Dedicated gives much more predictable SLOs — we'll include target numbers in the parity sheet and propose a dedicated trial if you need low-tailed latency.
[05:49] Leah: About caching — do you support prefix/KV caching? We often cache system prompts and partial contexts.

[05:56] Marco: Yes, automatic prefix and KV cache management is built into the runtime. We call it KV cash in some quick notes — sorry, transcript typo there — but yes KV cache, and we expose hooks for cache warmup.
[06:15] Daniel: Security checklist — SOC2, ISO, SSO?
[06:20] Priya: Redwood has SOC 2, SSO/SAML support, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations for Private/Dedicated. We'll send the security questionnaire and compliance pack after the call.
[06:38] Sara (Procurement): From a procurement angle, can you share standard T&Cs and data processing addendum?
[06:45] Alyssa: Yes — we'll attach our DPA and a redline-friendly contract template with the pricing email.

[07:00] Marco: Back to migration specifics — here's a side-by-side snippet: OpenAI chat completion -> Redwood generate; streaming is chunked but we support delta updates for UI. For function calling, we map schema -> tools and return structured call objects.
[07:26] Leah: Are there any known gotchas moving from Anthropic? We've seen some temperature + sampling behavior differences.

[07:34] Marco: Right — Anthropic-style models sometimes have different sampling default. We recommend running the same eval prompts and compare outputs; Optimize can detect quality regressions over time.
[07:52] Daniel: Cost modelling — do you provide a calculator?
[07:57] Alyssa: We'll include an initial cost comparison in the parity spreadsheet with sample traffic numbers; Optimize gives recommendations like batching and quantization to hit cost targets.
[08:12] Marco: Also show Console > Optimize: it suggests quantization profiles and batching thresholds based on sample latency histograms; you can simulate cost savings before applying.
[08:30] Leah: On embeddings — vector dims and model drift. If we switch models will our index be invalidated?

[08:37] Marco: Good question — different embedding models give different vector spaces. We recommend re-embedding in the POC window; Console supports reindexing and can keep old index if you want A/B tests.
[08:58] Omar: Networking — for Private on-prem we might be air-gapped; is there an installable package?
[09:04] Priya: Yes, we have an on-prem package for regulated setups. It includes local control plane and integrates with your KMS/HSM. We'll add the install notes to the security doc.
[09:20] Daniel: Ok can you walk through a small code example for migrating a streaming chat using our existing client?

[09:26] Marco: Sure — here's a snippet. (reads code) You basically switch the endpoint and map the message shape; for streaming you listen to the same chunk events. We'll paste the sample repo after the call.
[10:05] Leah: Do you have any automated test harness for regression testing? We run evals across 500 prompts nightly.

[10:12] Marco: We have an evals harness integrated into Console; you can upload prompts and expected outputs, and it will run periodic evals and raise regression alerts. We can run your prompt set in the POC.
[10:34] Daniel: How about rate limiting and quotas? We have spikes and need graceful throttling.
[10:39] Marco: Rate limiting per key and per-route with backoff headers. Also automatic fallback to a cheaper model if quota exceeded can be set in routing policies.

[11:02] Alyssa: Let's pivot to the POC plan — propose 1 week of real traffic testing or replay with 10k requests/day equivalent. We'll run benchmarks for latency and cost, and compare outputs for N prompt sets.
[11:18] Leah: That works. We'll provide the prompt sets, traffic profile, and acceptance criteria — F1 for retrieval and exact-match thresholds for structured outputs.
[11:28] Marco: For benchmarks we'll need a sample key, traffic replay details, and a bucket for logs. Note: logs will be redacted per our DPA.
[11:45] Omar: On Dedicated — how quickly can we spin up reserved capacity? We have a Q2 window.
[11:52] Priya: Dedicated provisioning depends on capacity and region; typical lead is 2–4 weeks for GA configs. For faster start we recommend hosted POC then move to Dedicated once we prove perf.
[12:08] Daniel: Any thoughts about model mismatches for few-shot prompts? We've tuned prompts heavily for OpenAI chat completion tokenization behavior.
[12:16] Marco: Few-shot can behave slightly differently; best practice is to include the same examples and run evals. Optimize will suggest prompt-level changes if we detect consistent shifts.
[12:35] Leah: Can Redwood replicate OpenAI's token counting for cost forecasting?
[12:41] Marco: We show token-level cost breakdowns in the Console and give an estimation tool, but tokenization differences might cause small deltas; we'll surface those in the parity spreadsheet.
[12:58] Daniel: Let's discuss the acceptance criteria for the POC — what do you typically measure?
[13:05] Marco: Latency p50/p95, token cost, embedding recall for top-k, and structured output accuracy. We'll propose thresholds and you can adjust.
[13:20] Alyssa: Quick logistics: Sara, procurement — we'll send contracts and standard pricing. Daniel, Leah — we'll need prompts and traffic by Friday.
[13:32] Sara: We'll review contracts; please include any pass-through compliance costs.
[13:38] Alyssa: Will do. Any other questions?
[13:44] Leah: One more re caching — you mentioned hooks for cache warmup. Can you give a quick example?
[13:50] Marco: We have an API that primes KV cache with common prefixes and can pre-warm embeddings indices. We'll include the warmup sample in the repo.
[14:05] Daniel: Great — I think that's everything from us. Let's confirm the deliverables and owners.

[14:11] Alyssa: Recap: Alyssa — pricing & parity sheet, Marco — bench checklist + sample code, Priya — security pack, Leah — prompt sets, Omar — network constraints. We'll aim to kick off POC week starting 2026-04-13.
[14:30] Marco: Quick note — in the parity doc we'll mark exact API mappings, expected behavioral diffs, and recommended default flags (sampling, temperature, top_p equivalents).
[14:44] Daniel: Perfect. Thanks everyone — we'll look out for the email.
[14:48] Alyssa: Thanks — we'll follow up by 2026-04-03. Bye!
[51:10] [call end — recording stopped]
